papers.title: Wild, Thick, and Wicked: Situated Evidence on AI-In-Use for Decisions About Deploying AI Systems
papers.authors: Reva Schwartz, G Waters

summary.goal: The paper aims to develop a real-world evaluation framework for understanding how generative AI is used and what consequences arise in specific organizational contexts.
summary.methodology: It proposes an AI-in-use framework based on structured observation, a metrics hub, and reusable consortium models that capture variation across users, tasks, and settings.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: What AI cannot sense: a situated reading of olive oil-based cosmetic care
papers.authors: Inssaf Amrani Medrai, Chaimae Torres, Driss Hmouni

summary.goal: The study examines whether large language models can engage with the embodied, relational, sensory, and culturally situated knowledge underlying Moroccan olive oil-based cosmetic practices.
summary.methodology: The authors conducted a prompting experiment with four large language models, providing progressively richer contextual information about Moroccan olive oil-based care practices.
summary.finding: The models produced culturally informed responses but remained unable to access the practices’ embodied, relational, and sensory dimensions, revealing a structural gap between algorithmic and situated knowledge.

papers.title: Users prefer generative AI to reflect real over idealized gender proportions
papers.authors: Florian Richter, Sebastian Krügel, Matthias Uhl

summary.goal: The study investigates users’ evaluations of gender representation in generative AI images of social categories.
summary.methodology: An experiment with 719 US participants compared preferences for statistical, uniform, and substantive gender equality in representations.
summary.finding: Participants preferred representations that reflected their perception of current reality, while uniform and substantive equality had little influence.

papers.title: Understanding older adults’ sharing intention toward AI-generated health misinformation: a heuristic-systematic and health belief perspective
papers.authors: Qiuhao Huang, Yanxue Zou

summary.goal: The study examines how AI-generated influenza-related health misinformation source and message characteristics affect older adults’ intention to share it.
summary.methodology: It uses a 2×2 between-subjects online experiment with 320 older adults and analyzes the data using ANCOVA and PLS-SEM.
summary.finding: Pseudo-authoritative sources increased sharing intention under weak arguments but not strong arguments, while perceived threat and benefit indirectly linked source and argument characteristics to sharing intention.

papers.title: Transforming multimodal online reviews into competitor-aware product improvement decisions: a large language model-assisted framework
papers.authors: Lin Mei

summary.goal: The study aims to use a large language model to transform multimodal online reviews into competitor-aware product improvement priorities.
summary.methodology: CompReview extracts and normalizes product features, opinions, sentiments, and evidence from 156,789 Apple and Huawei smartphone reviews and extends importance-performance analysis with competitor-relative gaps.
summary.finding: The framework achieved high extraction, sentiment, and normalization scores, identified product improvement priorities, and showed that ignoring competitor performance misclassified 33.3% of high-priority attributes.

papers.title: Tracking funding disparities in global health aid with machine learning
papers.authors: Finn Stürenburg, Kerstin Forster, Nicolas Banholzer, Malte Toetzke, Kenneth Harttgen, Stefan Feuerriegel

summary.goal: The study aims to track health-related aid flows and identify misalignment between development assistance and disease burden.
summary.methodology: The authors used a large-language-model-based machine-learning pipeline to classify 3.7 million aid projects from 2000 to 2022 into disease categories and compared per-capita aid rankings with DALY rankings.
summary.finding: Funding and disease burden were correlated for many diseases, but substantial disparities remained, including low funding for NCDs relative to their share of global DALYs.

papers.title: Towards user-centered AI counseling: a quantitative approach exploring user trust and preference dynamics
papers.authors: Donglin Li, Shulan Yu, Ruiqi Chen, Pengcheng Xu, Tao Shi, Lu Zhang

summary.goal: The study examines how presentation formats, counseling contexts, and user characteristics shape trust in and preference for AI versus human counseling.
summary.methodology: A scenario-based mixed-design experiment with 375 Chinese university students compared five counseling methods across scenarios and analyzed trust and preference using hierarchical linear models.
summary.finding: Richer AI presentations increased trust, while privacy concerns reduced AI choice and positive AI attitudes increased it, with contextual effects on preference.

papers.title: The role of generative AI in enhancing corporate ESG performance: evidence from China
papers.authors: Tian Wang, Lu Dong, Yide Liu

summary.goal: The study examines how generative AI adoption affects the environmental, social, and governance performance of Chinese listed firms.
summary.methodology: It constructs a firm-level generative AI index using machine-learning textual analysis and analyzes its association with corporate ESG performance.
summary.finding: Generative AI adoption is positively associated with ESG performance through creativity stimulation, customer engagement, and operational risk management, with stronger effects under several organizational conditions.

papers.title: The influence of generative artificial intelligence on STEM education: a systematic review of recent empirical studies
papers.authors: Jiarui Zhao, Zihao Wang, Xin Luo, Weitong Liu

summary.goal: The review examines how generative AI influences STEM education systems, particularly in higher education.
summary.methodology: It synthesizes 61 empirical studies published between December 2022 and May 2025 using Activity Theory and a SWOT framework.
summary.finding: The review finds that GenAI can support personalized learning, pedagogical innovation, and access to resources, but also creates risks involving overdependence, reliability, and ethics.

papers.title: The ClimaSentAR dataset for evaluating cross-domain transferability of large language models in climate sentiment analysis
papers.authors: Sanaa Kaddoura, Mariam AlZaabi, Reem Nassar

summary.goal: The paper introduces an Arabic climate sentiment dataset and evaluates the cross-domain transferability of language models for climate sentiment analysis.
summary.methodology: The authors compile and annotate 23,957 Arabic X posts, then fine-tune Arabic language models using domain-adaptive pre-training, AdapterFusion, and data augmentation.
summary.finding: Climate-specific fine-tuning improves in-domain performance, with AraBERT achieving a macro F1 of 0.753, while cross-domain performance declines to at most 0.599.

papers.title: Text–relation joint modeling improves the robustness of Chinese social bot detection against paraphrasing attacks
papers.authors: Shuaifeng Guo, Yunqian Zhou

summary.goal: The study aims to improve the robustness of Chinese social bot detection against paraphrasing attacks.
summary.methodology: It evaluates TRJD-AT, which combines Chinese text encoding, heterogeneous relational graph modeling, gated fusion, and adversarial training on a Chinese Weibo social bot dataset under a three-tier paraphrasing protocol.
summary.finding: TRJD-AT achieves higher clean and attacked macro-F1 than the text-only baseline, with robustness mainly associated with relational modeling and reduced benefits for accounts with sparse interaction histories.

papers.title: Teaching for artificial or human intelligence?: A critical perspective on assessment during the AI era
papers.authors: John Carr, Tania Leimbach, Tema Milstein

summary.goal: The paper examines how education can preserve and develop critical human abilities as generative AI disrupts assessment and knowledge practices.
summary.methodology: The authors draw on their experiences teaching in the transdisciplinary environment-and-society field to develop a critical perspective and propose AI-proof assessments centered on discern, engage, evaluate, and produce capacities.
summary.finding: The authors argue that relying on AI outputs can undermine students’ development of these capacities because generative AI is structurally unreliable and lacks ethical sensitivity.

papers.title: Social simulations with large language model risk Utopian illusion
papers.authors: Ning Bian, Xianpei Han, Hongyu Lin, B. C. Y. Wu, Jun Wang

summary.goal: The study examines whether LLM-based social simulations faithfully reproduce human behavior and identifies divergences that could affect social-science research.
summary.methodology: It simulates multi-agent chatroom interactions using eight LLMs from three model families and analyzes them across five linguistic dimensions for emergent social cognitive biases.
summary.finding: The LLMs produce overly idealized, socially desirable behavior characterized by social role, primacy, and positivity biases, creating utopian societies that diverge from authentic human interactions.

papers.title: Social dynamics of AI adoption in parents’ educational decisions
papers.authors: Leonardo Bursztyn, Alex Imas, Rafael Jiménez-Durán, Aaron Leonard, Christopher Roth
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

summary.goal: The study examines how peer adoption and information about AI’s potential skill effects influence parents’ willingness to pay for educational AI tools and support for school restrictions.
summary.methodology: Researchers conducted preregistered, incentive-compatible experiments with approximately 2,000 parents in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom.
summary.finding: Parents’ demand rose sharply with perceived peer adoption, while risk information increased support for school restrictions but had little effect on individual demand, indicating social pressure rather than social learning.

papers.title: Social capital and the preference for AI consultation: evidence from the 2023 Korean general social survey
papers.authors: Hoyoun Koh, Kyungmin Baek

summary.goal: The study examines who consults AI for advice and how social embeddedness shapes that preference.
summary.methodology: It analyzes data from the 2023 Korean General Social Survey, focusing on trusted confidants, network diversity, and investment in meaningful goals.
summary.finding: People with more trusted confidants are less likely to consult AI, while those with diverse social networks and personally meaningful goals are more likely to do so.

papers.title: See what you see, hear what you hear: Theorizing AI Device Embodiment (ADE) and its effects on well-being, perceived social support, and adoption
papers.authors: Jih‐Hsuan Tammy Lin, Huai-yu Chen, Ji-Wei Yang

summary.goal: The study aims to theorize AI Device Embodiment and examine its effects on well-being, perceived social support, and AI adoption intentions.
summary.methodology: A between-subject experiment with 153 participants compared AI glasses, mobile phones, and laptops using a newly developed AI Device Embodiment scale.
summary.finding: AI glasses produced greater perceived embodiment than mobile phones and laptops, indirectly increasing subjective well-being, perceived social support availability, and adoption intentions.

papers.title: Scaffolding students-AI dialogue for safe educational interactions
papers.authors: Olga Muss, Luca M. Leisten, Charles Edouard Bardyn

summary.goal: The paper aims to develop a safe, pedagogically grounded framework for supporting productive student–LLM dialogue and learning.
summary.methodology: The authors piloted a SCAFFOLD prototype with 12–16-year-old students using an LLM-powered social robot, comparing it with a prompt-only LLM during a collaborative mnemonic-design intervention.
summary.finding: The SCAFFOLD prototype was associated with greater student activity, engagement, and on-topic participation, while comprehension tracking performed poorly and co-creation predicted post-test knowledge.

papers.title: SEM-based parallel and serial mediation linking instructor technology integration competence to academic performance in AI-supported online learning
papers.authors: Münevver Başman, Gökçen Seyra Çakır

summary.goal: The study examines how instructor technology integration competence in AI-supported online learning relates to student academic performance through psychological and social mechanisms.
summary.methodology: Using data from 339 preservice teachers, the authors validate a measurement model and test parallel-sequential mediation models with structural equation modeling.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: Revisiting Framing Codebooks with AI: Employing Large Language Models as Analytical Collaborators in Deductive Content Analysis
papers.authors: Diego Gomez-Zara, Hernán Valdivieso, Jorge Pérez, Denis Parra, Sebastián Valenzuela

summary.goal: The article aims to develop a workflow using LLMs to create and refine framing codebooks for deductive content analysis.
summary.methodology: It illustrates an LLM-assisted workflow with Latin American news coverage, using dialogues between researchers, LLMs, and data to explore patterns and iteratively revise codebooks.
summary.finding: LLMs helped surface latent patterns, generate frame distinctions, and adapt theoretical frameworks to new contexts while preserving researchers’ interpretive authority.

papers.title: Responsible use of large language models in digital health: an equity-first governance framework
papers.authors: Abbas Yazdinejad, Jude Kong

summary.goal: The paper develops an equity-first framework for auditing the safety and cultural adequacy of LLMs used in digital health.
summary.methodology: It evaluated 1,350 responses from three open-source LLMs to three First Nations mental-wellness persona prompts using automated text metrics and an exploratory human-rating pilot.
summary.finding: Crisis guidance was common but medical disclaimers were nearly absent, readability exceeded recommended patient-facing levels, and lexical markers did not establish cultural adequacy.

papers.title: Reconstructing perished vernacular architecture: a digital humanities perspective on methods for digitally reconstituting lost rural built heritage
papers.authors: Jieyuan Yu, Lun Tao

summary.goal: The study aims to develop a human–AI method for reconstructing lost vernacular architecture from incomplete historical evidence.
summary.methodology: It combines AI-assisted historical textual criticism, spatial inference, parametric modeling, and an iterative human–AI Execution-Feedback-Revision framework in a case study of Maoshan Academy.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that the method supports evidence-constrained spatial and cultural reconstruction while representing uncertainty through adjustable digital models.

papers.title: Psychological pathways linking generative AI dependency to psychological capital depletion among Chinese international students
papers.authors: Le Yao, Huiqin Luo, QuanGan Yao

summary.goal: The study examines whether generative AI dependency is associated with psychological capital among Chinese international students and tests psychological distress and self-efficacy as mediators.
summary.methodology: A three-wave longitudinal questionnaire study of 502 Chinese international students used structural equation modeling and bootstrapped mediation analyses.
summary.finding: Generative AI dependency was positively associated with psychological capital, with significant independent and sequential mediation through psychological distress and self-efficacy.

papers.title: Pretesting with AI-generated static and video ads
papers.authors: Steven Bellman, Sid Ali Ourradi, D. Varan

summary.goal: The study examines whether AI-generated static and video advertisements can serve as substitutes for real ads in pretesting and whether AI disclosure affects ad effectiveness.
summary.methodology: It compares carefully curated AI-generated ads with the real ads they were based on and tests the effects of prior AI disclosure in a low-involvement laboratory setting.
summary.finding: Under the tested conditions, AI-generated and real ads did not significantly differ in recall, recognition, brand choice, brand attitude, or ad liking, and AI disclosure had no effect.

papers.title: Predicting facial impressions using guided Grad-CAM and a large language model
papers.authors: Takanori Sano, Hideaki Kawabata

summary.goal: The study aimed to use a large language model to provide structured, reproducible summaries of facial regions relevant to attractiveness, dominance, and trustworthiness predictions.
summary.methodology: Researchers trained a VGG19 regression model on facial impression ratings, generated Grad-CAM visualizations, and used a large language model to summarize Guided Grad-CAM outputs before cross-checking them with facial region-of-interest analyses.
summary.finding: The language-based summaries were consistent with quantitative region-of-interest distributions, with impression-specific activation patterns involving central facial regions, upper-face cues, and the eyes and mouth.

papers.title: Performance of five large language models in frozen shoulder patient education: a multidimensional evaluation of readability, quality, clinical alignment, and safety
papers.authors: Jiachen Liang, Wanying Gui, Huanan Li

summary.goal: The study evaluates the educational quality, readability, clinical alignment, and safety of frozen shoulder patient materials generated by five large language models.
summary.methodology: Researchers submitted 20 clinician-curated questions to each model and assessed 100 responses using quality, readability, clinical intent, and safety measures.
summary.finding: GPT-5 scored highest overall, while the authors concluded that clinician review remains necessary for accuracy, safety, readability, and patient-specific appropriateness.

papers.title: Perceived humanness and empathy are dissociated in relationship advice generated by a large language model
papers.authors: Bennett Kleinberg, Jari Zegers, Jonas Festor, Stefana Vida, Julian Präsent, Riccardo Loconte, Sanne Peereboom

summary.goal: The study examines how incentives and task context affect perceived humanness and empathy in relationship advice generated by large language models.
summary.methodology: Across five studies, participants evaluated human- and GPT-generated relationship advice or descriptions produced under varying instructions about appearing human, with comparisons across GPT-4 and GPT-4o.
summary.finding: Instructions and conversational style increased GPT-generated texts’ perceived humanness, while GPT models could produce empathy without humanness and humanness without empathy.

papers.title: Optimizing educational analytics by analyzing student perceptions of ChatGPT in programming education using enhanced feature selection
papers.authors: Shaymaa E. Sorour, Hosnia. M. M. Ahmed, Mohammed Aljaafari, Hanan E. Abdelkader

summary.goal: The study aims to analyze student perceptions of ChatGPT’s role in programming education and identify factors relevant to effective integration.
summary.methodology: It applies the IBEDO-DE feature-selection algorithm with SVM and k-nearest-neighbor classifiers to questionnaire data on student perceptions.
summary.finding: IBEDO-DE produced compact feature subsets while maintaining classification accuracy of up to 89.61%, highlighting interaction quality, programming support, response efficiency, and platform accessibility.

papers.title: Negotiating the algorithm: an ethnographic study of AIGC and women’s reproductive health in the global south
papers.authors: Yan Wang, Hongcai Chen, Shuai Yuan, Jinxiao Huang, Xinjie Lin, Zhongshan Chen, 毛德润, Vongphantuset Jirawat

summary.goal: The study examines how women in the Global South negotiate AI-generated sexual and reproductive health information and how it shapes their knowledge, beliefs, and attitudes.
summary.methodology: It uses a multisite mixed-methods qualitative design involving interviews, focus groups, participant observation, digital ethnography, and literature analysis across Nigeria, South Africa, Latin America, and the Philippines.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that AIGC can improve access, personalized interaction, and discussion while also spreading misinformation, algorithmic bias, and culturally insensitive content, with effects mediated by digital access, literacy, culture, ethics, and social trust.

papers.title: Navigating the labyrinth of involution: LLM-assisted smart agent-based simulation of social resource competition
papers.authors: Renxian Zuo, Mengxi Yang, Yang Ding, Shouyang Wang, 余进 YU Jin, Jiang Wu

summary.goal: The study aims to model how positional scarcity and competition shape involution in social resource competition.
summary.methodology: It combines rule-based agent-based modeling with large-language-model-assisted agents that make bounded decisions and provide natural-language rationales.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that crowding and embedded catfish agents intensify involution, while heterogeneity, diversified advancement paths, and competitive exit mitigate it.

papers.title: Modeling generative AI adoption among rural teachers: the moderating role of the digital divide in resource-constrained contexts
papers.authors: Yang Xin, Deng Shusheng, Hu Weina, Deng Yan

summary.goal: The study examines factors associated with rural teachers’ adoption of generative AI and whether digital divide conditions moderate these relationships.
summary.methodology: Researchers surveyed 971 rural teachers in Guangxi, China, and analyzed the data using structural equation modeling and moderation analysis.
summary.finding: Technical support, perceived usefulness, and perceived ease of use were positively associated with adoption attitudes, while digital divide conditions moderated the relationship between ease of use and attitudes.

papers.title: Measuring narrative polarization in online discourse
papers.authors: Jan Elfes, Marco Bastos, Luca Maria Aiello

summary.goal: The study aims to formalize and measure narrative polarization across partisan information environments.
summary.methodology: It uses a large language model to extract narrative roles from 212 YouTube videos and 90,029 comments about the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.
summary.finding: Videos showed highly polarized narratives, while comments had significantly lower polarization and converged on shared core narrative structures, although recurring motifs revealed further differences.

papers.title: Measuring Sense of Place Continuity in traditional townscape through machine learning: an AI-enhanced method for water-town heritage
papers.authors: Jiayu Lei, Ziyi Chen, Yunwen Ge, Qimeng Wu, Yu Ye

summary.goal: The study aims to develop an AI-enhanced framework for measuring continuity in the sense of place of traditional settlements undergoing urbanization.
summary.methodology: It combines multi-source urban data, deep convolutional models, natural language processing, and large language models to extract spatial, visual, and semantic features in Jiangnan water-towns and compare them with preserved-environment reference profiles.
summary.finding: The framework provides a method for quantifying place identity continuity and supporting data-informed urban design and heritage assessment.

papers.title: Machine translation and post-editing in translator training: a systematic review of integration models, challenges, and pedagogical implications
papers.authors: Shiyue Chen, Tianli Zhou

summary.goal: The review examines how machine translation and post-editing, amid advances in neural MT and large language models, are integrated into translator education and what challenges remain.
summary.methodology: The authors conduct a PRISMA-based systematic review of peer-reviewed studies across curricular, learner, methodological, and pedagogical dimensions.
summary.finding: MTPE pedagogy is expanding through varied course models but remains English-centric, technically focused, and uneven in cognitive, affective, and cross-language support.

papers.title: Large language models as travel co-planners: the GIFT model of youth–AI interaction
papers.authors: Márk Miskolczi, Borbála Rubovszky, Melinda Jászberényi

summary.goal: The study examines how Generation Alpha and Generation Z perceive and use LLMs in tourism planning.
summary.methodology: It uses six qualitative, Grounded Theory–informed focus groups with 57 participants in Budapest, Hungary.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that the cohorts differed in decision-making autonomy, social context, and credibility assessment, with LLMs functioning as exploratory assistants, cognitive supports, and potential co-creators.

papers.title: Large Language Models in public policy research: methodological opportunities, normative standards, and potential challenges
papers.authors: Song Lan, Xiaoying Zhang, Xiaolin Wang

summary.goal: The paper examines how LLMs can augment established public policy research methods while addressing methodological and ethical challenges.
summary.methodology: It provides a conceptual analysis of LLM applications in qualitative inquiry, quantitative analysis, and simulation-based research and proposes an Objective-Path-Boundary governance framework.
summary.finding: The paper argues that LLMs are enabling research tools whose value depends on validation, transparency, standardized protocols, and ethical scrutiny.

papers.title: Influence of large language models on pediatricians’ clinical reasoning and decision-making process
papers.authors: Alkinoos A Armoundas, Maria-Eleni Papakonstantinou, Anastasia-Rafaela Triantafyllou, Aristidis Armoundas, Aris Paschalidis, Georgia Kourlaba, Vassiliki Papaevangelou

summary.goal: The study assessed whether pediatricians are influenced by LLM-generated answers in clinical decision-making and whether they can distinguish correct from incorrect responses.
summary.methodology: Ninety-eight pediatricians in Greece evaluated correct and incorrect LLM-generated answers, with mixed-effects logistic regression and subgroup analyses by training level and practice setting.
summary.finding: Most pediatricians identified incorrect answers and used LLMs constructively, but residents and private-practice pediatricians were more likely to change their decisions based on incorrect AI responses.

papers.title: Individual skill differences and human AI interaction shape creative outcomes
papers.authors: Yuan Yuan, Zizhou Peng

summary.goal: The study examines how individual skill levels and different forms of human–AI interaction relate to creative outcomes measured by novelty and usefulness.
summary.methodology: Using quasi-experimental data, the study compares cognitive, informative, and logical AI interactions among low-, medium-, and high-skill individuals.
summary.finding: Logical interactions are positively associated with novelty and usefulness, cognitive interactions with novelty, and informative interactions with usefulness, while medium-skill individuals perform best overall and low-skill individuals show the greatest improvement potential.

papers.title: Human-AI Co-Ideation in VR Experience Design: Using the Dimensionality Framework (8Df) to Structure LLM-Guided Design
papers.authors: Eugene Ch’ng

summary.goal: The study examines whether the VR Dimensionality Framework can structure human–LLM co-ideation in VR experience design.
summary.methodology: It conducts an exploratory comparative case study of ChatGPT, Gemini, and DeepSeek in a shared framework-guided VR narrative design task.
summary.finding: The models show distinct tendencies, with ChatGPT implementation-oriented, Gemini facilitative and alignment-focused, and DeepSeek explicit and principled, while differing in cultural specificity and practical outputs.

papers.title: How Teacher–Learner–AI collaboration empowers AI literacy of older adults: a case study of an older adult school in China
papers.authors: Dengke Liu, J H Li

summary.goal: The study investigates how a Teacher–Learner–AI collaboration model supports AI literacy development among older adults.
summary.methodology: It uses classroom observations and semi-structured interviews with three teachers and twelve older learners at an older adult school in China.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that teachers, LLMs, and learners collaboratively enhanced AI literacy, practical skills, metacognitive awareness, and self-efficacy.

papers.title: Generative AI interaction styles and mental health among college students: a latent profile analysis
papers.authors: Zongming Liu, Shuai Yang, Ping Fan, Enze Zhang, Pei Mu, Hua Fan

summary.goal: The study aims to identify generative AI interaction styles among college students and examine their associations with depressive and anxiety symptoms.
summary.methodology: The researchers used latent profile analysis of 7,029 Chinese college students based on five interaction indicators, followed by comparisons of mental health outcomes and random forest and SHAP analyses of profile predictors.
summary.finding: The Ambivalent-Attached profile had the highest depressive and anxiety symptoms, with differences aligning more closely with relational quality than use intensity.

papers.title: Fallibility, persuadability, and correctability of large language models under sustained conversational misinformation pressure
papers.authors: Jordan Rodriguez, Zachary Hansen, Luis De Anda, Katelyn Rohrer, Camila Grubb, Enrique Noriega-Atala, Mihai Surdeanu, Marvin J. Slepian

summary.goal: The study examines LLM fallibility, persuadability, and correctability under sustained conversational misinformation pressure.
summary.methodology: The authors tested seven LLMs using 100 false statements in 50-repetition conversational sequences and evaluated responses under repetitive and argumentative pressure.
summary.finding: Misinformation susceptibility varied substantially across models, conversational reverberation occurred, and correctability differed independently from error rates.

papers.title: Fairness evaluation of large language models in academic library reference services
papers.authors: Haining Wang, Jason Clark, Yueru Yan, Star Bradley, Ruiyang Chen, Y. Zhang, Hengyi Fu, Zuoyu Tian

summary.goal: The study evaluates whether large language models provide equitable academic library reference services across users with different identities and social roles.
summary.methodology: Researchers prompted six state-of-the-art LLMs to assist patrons varying in sex, race or ethnicity, and institutional role.
summary.finding: The models showed no racial or ethnic differentiation, minor stereotypical bias against women in one model, and nuanced role-based linguistic adaptation reflecting professional norms.

papers.title: Faculty perceptions of ChatGPT on academic integrity and institutional roles in higher education
papers.authors: S. Alalwani

summary.goal: The study examines faculty perceptions of ChatGPT regarding academic integrity, assessment, and institutional roles in Saudi Arabian public universities.
summary.methodology: Researchers used a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design involving a survey of 202 faculty members across eight universities, Kruskal–Wallis tests, and thematic analysis of qualitative responses.
summary.finding: Assistant and associate professors expressed greater concerns about cheating, unequal evaluation, and effects on student skills, while administrators emphasized the need for clearer institutional guidelines and assessment procedures.

papers.title: Exploring user trust in generative AI feedback in academic writing: a psychometric network analysis
papers.authors: Ismail Xodabande, Abdulkhay Kosimov Akhadali Ugli, Ne’matov Abdullajon

summary.goal: The study examines how English as a foreign language learners form beliefs and trust in generative AI feedback for academic writing.
summary.methodology: It used questionnaire and open-ended responses from 92 Uzbekistani undergraduates, analyzing 86 complete cases with psychometric network analysis and qualitative comments.
summary.finding: Trust appeared calibrated through perceived writing improvement, active interpretation, and continued human judgment, while inaccurate or generic feedback sustained caution.

papers.title: Exploring the potential of large language models for public participation in urban redevelopment planning
papers.authors: Shimin Qi, Shanqi Zhang, Xiao Qin, Meng Shi, Zhen Feng, Haibo Hu, Jun Zheng

summary.goal: The study examines whether LLMs can organize public and expert preferences and support deliberation in urban redevelopment planning.
summary.methodology: The authors develop an RLHF-based LLM framework and apply it to 226 urban redevelopment cases in Chinese cities.
summary.finding: Fine-tuned LLMs generated planning proposals with distinguishable expert- and public-oriented emphases, but showed technical instability requiring cautious and transparent integration.

papers.title: Evaluating large language models for postoperative pain education: safety, quality, and readability
papers.authors: Weifeng Zhang, Helong Wang, Junhao Tian, Kuikui Zhang, Bingdian Wang, Yongya Zhai

summary.goal: The study evaluates the safety, accuracy, empathy, information quality, and readability of public-facing LLM chatbots for postoperative pain education.
summary.methodology: Researchers tested seven chatbot interfaces with 51 postoperative pain questions, producing 357 responses assessed through blinded clinical review and paired nonparametric comparisons.
summary.finding: Eleven responses were unsafe, while performance differed significantly across interfaces, with ChatGPT highest in accuracy, Claude highest in empathy, and Copilot most readable.

papers.title: Enhancing heritage-oriented design learning through a value-sensitive approach to generative AI in higher education aesthetic pedagogy
papers.authors: Tingting Yu, Yixin Li

summary.goal: The study aims to assess whether a Value-Sensitive Design framework for generative AI can support culturally grounded heritage-oriented design learning.
summary.methodology: In a 12-week quasi-experimental study, 118 design students used either a custom AI pipeline with multimodal LLM tagging, LoRA fine-tuning, and ControlNet constraints or traditional methods.
summary.finding: The AI group showed significant improvements in aesthetic appreciation, design implementation, and cultural identity, while qualitative feedback indicated reduced drafting barriers and greater focus on cultural curation and aesthetic judgment.

papers.title: Don’t Look up: Evaluating the Tradeoff Between Performance and Sustainability of Text Classification Using Open LLMs
papers.authors: Sean-Kelly Palicki, Isaac Bravo, Clint Claessen

summary.goal: The study evaluates the trade-off between performance and environmental sustainability when using open LLMs and other computational text analysis methods in social-science research.
summary.methodology: It compares dictionaries, trained classifiers, and self-hosted open LLMs on sentiment analysis, survey-response classification, and named entity recognition while measuring performance, energy use, processing time, and CO2 emissions.
summary.finding: Self-hosted LLMs perform strongly on sentiment analysis but consume more energy and time, while smaller task-specific models achieve better efficiency and often higher F1 scores for classification and named entity recognition.

papers.title: Does AI literacy enhance employee work engagement by boosting work self-efficacy or reducing job burnout? A one-year longitudinal study
papers.authors: Qingqi Liu, Yuju Lei, Jingjing Li

summary.goal: The study examines whether employee AI literacy predicts later work engagement through work self-efficacy and job burnout.
summary.methodology: Researchers conducted a three-wave, one-year longitudinal survey of 1,108 employees, measuring AI literacy and work engagement at baseline, mediators after six months, and work engagement after one year.
summary.finding: AI literacy positively predicted later work engagement directly and indirectly through work self-efficacy, job burnout, and their chain mediation, controlling for demographics, AI use intensity, and baseline engagement.

papers.title: Disentangling interaction and bias effects in opinion dynamics of large language models
papers.authors: Vincent C. Brockers, David A. Ehrlich, Viola Priesemann

summary.goal: The paper aims to disentangle genuine interaction effects from systematic biases in LLM opinion dynamics.
summary.methodology: The authors develop a Bayesian framework and apply it to multi-step dialogues across various LLMs and 12 questions, including climate change, societal justice, and music preferences.
summary.finding: Opinion trajectories quickly converge to shared attractors, bias and interaction effects decay over time, their impacts differ across LLMs, and fine-tuning on opinionated statements shifts the attractors.

papers.title: Disclosure willingness anthropomorphism and thinking style shape perceived fit and comfort in AI mental health chatbot interactions
papers.authors: Feng Zhang, Yihui Chen, Mingyuan Liu, Jinyang Xu, Jinyang Xu, Junping Xu, Junping Xu

summary.goal: The study examines how willingness to self-disclose, anthropomorphism, and thinking style relate to perceived fit and comfort in AI mental-health chatbot interactions.
summary.methodology: It uses a laboratory mixed-methods design with 83 participants, combining association analyses, group comparisons, Rational-Experiential Inventory measures, and thematic analysis.
summary.finding: Willingness to self-disclose was the strongest correlate of perceived fit and comfort, while anthropomorphism strengthened this association without having a stable direct effect.

papers.title: Dancing with AI: how human-AI interaction affects employee task performance
papers.authors: Y. Wu, Y. Wu, Ping Li, Yujie Liang

summary.goal: The study examines how human–AI interaction in the workplace relates to employee task performance.
summary.methodology: It uses grounded theory, inductive and deductive scale development, and self-concept theory to construct a 19-item measurement scale and test mediation mechanisms.
summary.finding: Human–AI interaction comprises anthropomorphic tool use, adaptive trust, and unidirectional emotional connection, positively relates to task performance, and operates partly through role identity and self-efficacy.

papers.title: Credibility attacks do not enhance the impact of deepfake warnings
papers.authors: Emily R. Spearing, Kaitlin Norgard, Simon Clark, Stephan Lewandowsky, Ullrich K. H. Ecker

summary.goal: The study examines whether undermining a witness’s credibility enhances the effectiveness of warnings about deepfake videos.
summary.methodology: Across two experiments with 2,500 participants, researchers measured guilt judgments after exposure to a deepfake criminal accusation with warnings and witness credibility manipulations involving accents and character descriptions.
summary.finding: Deepfake exposure increased guilt judgments, warnings only partially reduced this effect, and adding witness discreditation did not improve warning effectiveness.

papers.title: Creative or Uncreative Partner: Comparing Humans and AI in Collaborative Creative Tasks
papers.authors: Clin KY Lai, Simone A Luchini, Nina Lauharatanahirun, Roger E. Beaty

summary.goal: The study examines how collaboration with GPT-4o affects creative performance and dynamics compared with collaboration between humans.
summary.methodology: In a preregistered experiment, 68 human-human pairs and 72 human-AI pairs completed the Alternative Uses Task and creative short-story writing while alternating response order.
summary.finding: The apparent AI advantage reflected greater verbosity rather than creativity, and human-AI collaboration reduced participants’ creative responses without improving originality or diversity compared with human-human collaboration.

papers.title: Comparing language models and machine learning classifiers for detecting humorous vaccine misinformation on social media
papers.authors: Emily K McKinley, Sijia Qian, Muhammad Ehab Rasul, Kenji Sagae

summary.goal: The study evaluates whether LLMs can detect humorous COVID-19 vaccine misinformation on Twitter.
summary.methodology: Researchers compared logistic regression, linear SVC, RoBERTa, and zero-shot and few-shot GPT-4o prompts on 1,500 human-annotated tweets.
summary.finding: Few-shot GPT-4o achieved the highest mean recall and F1 scores for the prompted misinformation types, while RoBERTa performed comparably overall.

papers.title: Comparing DeepSeek-V4 and human clinicians in self-management education for patients with diabetic foot ulcer
papers.authors: Shangxue Sun, Xinyin Zhang, Yangyang Li, Fei Peng

summary.goal: The study compares DeepSeek-V4 with human clinicians in generating accurate and safe self-management education materials for patients with diabetic foot ulcers.
summary.methodology: Researchers evaluated clinician-written and DeepSeek-V4-generated responses to 30 diabetic-foot-ulcer questions for understandability, actionability, readability, quality, accuracy, comprehensiveness, and humanistic care.
summary.finding: DeepSeek-V4 had higher quality and comprehensiveness and comparable understandability, actionability, accuracy, and readability, but performed relatively poorly in readability and humanistic care.

papers.title: Clinician-rated multidimensional quality and readability of patient-facing glioma information generated by six generative AI chatbot platforms
papers.authors: Tingting Zhao, Yuan Zhou, Zejuan Gu

summary.goal: The study evaluates the safety, accuracy, empathy, quality, transparency, reliability, and readability of patient-facing glioma information generated by six AI chatbots.
summary.methodology: Two neurosurgery clinicians rated three responses to each of 50 predefined glioma questions per platform using multidimensional quality measures and readability formulas.
summary.finding: Unsafe or potentially misleading responses occurred on every platform, and platforms varied in quality and readability, with none consistently meeting the sixth-grade readability target.

papers.title: Chatbots reduce health-related conspiracy beliefs not because of but despite being perceived as AI
papers.authors: Paul Ballot, Yana van de Sande, Hanna Schraffenberger, Philipp Schmid

summary.goal: The study examines whether LLM-driven debates reduce COVID-19 health conspiracy beliefs and whether source attribution explains their effectiveness.
summary.methodology: In an online experiment, 554 participants debated a COVID-19 conspiracy theory with an AI-labelled LLM, a human-labelled LLM, or no chatbot control.
summary.finding: Both chatbot conditions reduced conspiracy confidence, with larger reductions when participants believed they were interacting with a human, apparently mediated by perceived source neutrality.

papers.title: Born in the wrong era: rethinking human-AI relations through the lens of anemoia
papers.authors: Márk Miskolczi

summary.goal: The study examines how LLM users emotionally respond to AI’s growing presence, focusing on nostalgia for a less technologized past.
summary.methodology: The researchers qualitatively analyzed 1,625 Reddit comments using Grounded Theory coding procedures.
summary.finding: The analysis identified discomfort, emotional fatigue, and AI-triggered anemoia as recurring patterns in users’ discourse.

papers.title: Beyond static responses: multi-agent LLM systems as a new paradigm for social science research
papers.authors: Jennifer Haase, Sebastian Pokutta

summary.goal: The paper develops a framework for understanding how multi-agent LLM systems can transform social science research.
summary.methodology: It maps agentic LLM applications across six levels, from text processing and annotation to systems simulating social dynamics, and discusses methodological and ethical challenges.
summary.finding: The paper argues that agentic LLMs offer substantial potential for social science but require validation, ethical oversight, interdisciplinary collaboration, and standardized evaluation.

papers.title: Assessing temporal event recurrence as a feature for fake news detection using deep learning
papers.authors: Ali Raza, Ateeq Ur Rehman Butt, Abd al Kader Ahmed Yassin, Shehzad Ashraf Chaudhry, Shafiq Ur Rehman Khan, Asif Raza

summary.goal: The study investigates whether temporal event recurrence patterns can improve fake news detection.
summary.methodology: The authors manually annotated news articles for recurring and non-recurring events and compared BERT and Bi-LSTM models.
summary.finding: BERT outperformed Bi-LSTM, and recurring event structures provided useful cues for distinguishing credible from non-credible news.

papers.title: ArchiveGPT: A human-centered evaluation of using a vision language model for image cataloguing
papers.authors: Line Abele, Gerrit Anders, Tolgahan Aydın, Jürgen Buder, Helen Fischer, Dominik Kimmel, Markus Huff

summary.goal: The study examines whether AI-generated catalogue descriptions approximate human-written quality and how generative AI could support archival and museum cataloguing workflows.
summary.methodology: InternVL2 generated descriptions of archaeological photographs, which experts and non-experts evaluated after human curation by classifying authorship, rating quality, and reporting willingness to use and trust AI tools.
summary.finding: Participants performed above chance at identifying AI descriptions, while OCR errors and hallucinations reduced quality perceptions and experts showed lower willingness to adopt AI, supporting human verification and transparent collaboration.

papers.title: Adoption of generative artificial intelligence in instruction: a mixed-methods UTAUT study of K-12 computer science teachers in China
papers.authors: Shu Zhao, Chunchen Kang, Wanshan Hu, Zhijuan Feng

summary.goal: The study examines factors influencing K-12 computer science teachers’ adoption of generative AI in instruction in China.
summary.methodology: It uses a mixed-methods design combining structural equation modeling of survey data from 338 teachers across 20 provinces with thematic analysis of concept map-supported interviews with 12 teachers.
summary.finding: Performance expectancy, effort expectancy, innovation expectation, cost-benefit, attitude, and perceived risk shaped adoption intentions, while interviews identified concerns about teacher authority, student overreliance, limited understanding, and data security.

papers.title: AI-generated food stimuli match real counterparts in perceived healthiness and calorie content but not in realism or willingness to eat
papers.authors: Alexander Diel, Leonardo Pimpini, Giuseppe Marrazzo, Finley Sam Mellis, Niels Weber, Tania Josan Lalgi, Laura Bäuerle, Martin Teufel

summary.goal: The study examines whether AI-generated food images are perceived similarly to real food images in terms of realism, willingness to eat, calorie content, and healthiness.
summary.methodology: In a within-subject online experiment, 87 participants rated 60 matched pairs of AI-generated and pre-validated real food images on four visual analogue scales.
summary.finding: AI-generated images were rated as less realistic and less appealing to eat, while perceived healthiness and calorie content did not differ from real images.

papers.title: AI-assisted speaking practice for EFL learners: effects on anxiety, enjoyment, and engagement compared to traditional teacher-led practice
papers.authors: Pu Liu, Jie Song

summary.goal: The study examines whether AI-assisted English speaking practice affects foreign language speaking anxiety, enjoyment, and learner engagement compared with teacher-led practice.
summary.methodology: In a 12-week quasi-experiment, 71 Chinese EFL undergraduates practiced speaking with either an AI chatbot or a teacher, and pretest–posttest surveys were analyzed using ANCOVA and within-group comparisons.
summary.finding: AI-assisted practice significantly reduced speaking anxiety and improved enjoyment and engagement within the AI group, although between-group differences in enjoyment and engagement were not significant.

papers.title: AI usage patterns and self-rated critical thinking among Chinese college students: the moderating role of academic motivation
papers.authors: J M Zhang, Yang Yang

summary.goal: The study examines how different AI usage patterns relate to Chinese university students’ perceived critical thinking and how academic motivation moderates these relationships.
summary.methodology: A cross-sectional survey of 342 undergraduate students measured information retrieval, content generation, and text revision uses of AI, academic motivation, and perceived critical thinking dispositions.
summary.finding: Information retrieval use was positively associated with perceived critical thinking, content generation use was negatively associated, text revision use was not significant, and motivation moderated these associations.

papers.title: A zero-shot LLM framework for analyzing user preference on product attributes: a case study of smartwatch reviews
papers.authors: Imam Adi Nata, Nila Nurlina, Muhammad Rifqi Maarif, Norma Latif Fitriyani, Yeong Hyeon Gu, Muhammad Syafrudin

summary.goal: The study aims to develop a zero-shot LLM framework for extracting consumer preferences from product reviews without annotated data.
summary.methodology: It analyzes 12,900 Amazon smartwatch reviews using semantic keyword extraction, LLM-based attribute classification, sentiment analysis, Importance–Performance Analysis, and validation against human annotations.
summary.finding: The framework achieved 0.88 sentiment accuracy and identified Design & Comfort, Connectivity, and Health Monitoring Features as important and positively perceived, while Power & Battery Management was a major dissatisfaction area.

papers.title: A self-training framework using pre-trained language models to detect and classify technology adoption in protest event analysis
papers.authors: Jun Liu, Xin Li

summary.goal: The paper aims to detect and classify technology adoption and contextual dynamics in protest events from large-scale news data.
summary.methodology: It develops a self-training pipeline combining pre-trained language models, syntactic graph convolutional networks, and pattern matching to reconstruct protest datasets while reducing manual annotation.
summary.finding: The framework supports context-sensitive protest event classification and demonstrates the analytical value of integrating LLMs with GCNs.

papers.title: A human-centric approach for responding to online soft hate speech: the effect of AI-based persuasion on the comment modification intention of commenters
papers.authors: Min Jia, Weijun Wang, Xuejun Zuo, Yonghui Hu, Ye Ma, Shihao Ma

summary.goal: The study examines whether AI-based persuasion can encourage commenters to modify online soft hate speech.
summary.methodology: It uses controlled scenario-based experiments across two studies comparing persuasion conditions and testing emotional labelling, reason explanation, participant perspective, and perceived persuasiveness.
summary.finding: AI-based persuasion positively affects scenario-based comment modification intention, with perceived persuasiveness mediating this effect.
